_about: The single source of truth for every mechanic term. codex is the rule as the player reads it; design.fantasy is the pitch and design.holes what the mechanic does not do yet. docs/vocabulary.md is generated from this file by tools/export_vocabulary.gd. status: implemented (in sim/), planned (designed, not coded), idea (floated, undecided).

entries.name: Hull
entries.codex: Damage that gets past shield removes hull. Hull never recovers during a battle. At zero the mech is a wreck to be salvaged after the battle.

design.fantasy: The machine itself. When it is gone, the machine is a wreck.

entries.name: Shield
entries.codex: Enemy damage removes shield before hull. Shield components add shield up to the chassis maximum. Shields recharge fully between skirmishes.

design.fantasy: A buffer that buys you a few rounds to solve the squad before it starts costing you the machine.
design.holes: Option not coded: recharge only during phases spent out of combat.

entries.name: Heat
entries.codex: Attack components may add heat. Heat above the chassis maximum spills into hull damage one for one. Vent components remove heat.

design.fantasy: Every gun has a price, and the big ones are paid in smoke.
design.holes: Heat does nothing below the cap. Consider effects at high heat short of overflow.

entries.name: Reroll
entries.codex: Three rerolls per round, each rerolling every unlocked, unspent mech die. A reroll always lands on a different component: never the one showing, never one equivalent to it (a die whose components are all alike keeps what it shows). Rerolls may be spent before or after attacking, so a low damage roll is information for the rest of the round. Never pooled across rounds.

design.fantasy: You do not like what you see. You get three chances to change your mind, and the machine never shows you the same thing twice.

entries.name: Rift Pressure
entries.codex: Ticks once per battlefield phase and once per skirmish round. When full it resets and a fresh squad emerges at the rift.

design.fantasy: The city is running out of time, and there is a bar on screen that says so.
design.holes: Spawns a fixed squad. Should draw from the battle's faction and escalate.

entries.name: Gate Integrity
entries.codex: A squad whose path reaches the gate strikes it instead of moving. Gate integrity persists across battles and is repaired in the meta.

design.fantasy: The last wall of mankind. If it falls the campaign is over.
design.holes: Gate damage formula is a placeholder (strength divided by three).

entries.name: Attack face
entries.codex: Spend on a foe within reach to deal its power in damage, then apply its keywords and heat.

design.fantasy: A gun, a claw, a shell. The primary icon is its reach.

entries.name: Shield face
entries.codex: Spend on self or an ally to add its power in shield, capped at that mech's shield maximum.

design.fantasy: Raise the plating. Yours or a friend's.

entries.name: Vent face
entries.codex: Spend on self or an ally to remove its power in heat.

design.fantasy: Blow the heat out of the reactor before it blows out of the hull.

entries.name: Cracked component
entries.codex: A cracked component still acts but loses all modifiers: keywords, crit chance and unique effect. A destroyed component is blank and does nothing when it comes up. Both persist until repaired in the hangar.

design.fantasy: Something inside is broken and the die shows it.

entries.name: Damage range
entries.codex: A kinetic attack component shows a minimum and a maximum and rolls between them when spent, immediately and visibly. Energy components show one number and never roll. Numbers are in tens.

design.fantasy: Kinetic weapons do not promise. They roll.
design.holes: Ranges are content-authored per component; no upgrade path raises min or max yet.

entries.name: Critical hit
entries.codex: A kinetic component may carry a crit chance. On a crit the roll is doubled before other multipliers. Energy components never crit. Crits fire the on_crit passive trigger.

design.fantasy: Sometimes the round finds the seam.
design.holes: No crit-chance upgrades yet; no visible crit chance on the die face beyond the description.

entries.name: Melee
entries.codex: Targets any front-rank foe, and any back-rank foe whose column is exposed.

design.fantasy: Up close and personal.

entries.name: Line of fire
entries.codex: Targets any front-rank foe, and any back-rank foe whose column is exposed.

design.fantasy: If you can see it, you can shoot it. If something is in the way, shoot that first.

entries.name: Indirect
entries.codex: Targets any foe in either rank. Hitting the front rank triggers danger close.

design.fantasy: Over the wall and onto the thing behind it. Just do not aim it at your own feet.

entries.name: Cleave
entries.codex: Also hits the foes in the neighbouring columns of the target's rank.

design.fantasy: One swing, three ghouls.

entries.name: Pierce
entries.codex: Also hits the foe in the other rank of the target's column.

design.fantasy: The railgun does not care who is standing in front of whom.

entries.name: Burn
entries.codex: Adds one burn stack per 20 damage dealt, rounded up. Each round the foe takes 10 per stack, then loses one stack.

design.fantasy: Set it alight and let it think about its choices.

entries.name: Suppress
entries.codex: The target skips its telegraphed action this round.

design.fantasy: The big hit it was winding up never lands.

entries.name: Overcharge
entries.codex: Double the component's damage and double its heat.

design.fantasy: Push the reactor past the red line and hope the housing holds.

entries.name: Execute
entries.codex: Double damage against a foe at or below half its health.

design.fantasy: Finish it before it gets back up.

entries.name: Chain
entries.codex: Also hits the lowest-health foe within reach other than the target.

design.fantasy: The arc jumps to whoever looks weakest.

entries.name: Lock
entries.codex: After this component is spent, the die keeps it into next round instead of rolling.

design.fantasy: That roll was too good to let go.

entries.name: Steady
entries.codex: A ranged component with steady always deals its average instead of rolling. It may still crit.

design.fantasy: No surprises. That is the whole point of it.

entries.name: Flip
entries.codex: Set another mech's die to the face opposite its current one.

design.fantasy: Turn the die over. The other side is usually better.
design.holes: Needs a definition of opposite faces for non-d6 dice.

entries.name: Copy
entries.codex: Set this die to what an ally's die shows.

design.fantasy: Whatever they rolled, you rolled too.

entries.name: Reflect
entries.codex: While shield from this face remains, foes that strike this mech take damage equal to the component's power.

design.fantasy: Hit me. See what happens.
design.holes: Would need shield sources to be tracked separately.

entries.name: Burning
entries.codex: Foe status. See the burn keyword.

design.fantasy: On fire, and getting less on fire every round.

entries.name: Suppressed
entries.codex: Foe status. Skips its action this round, then clears.

design.fantasy: Head down, gun silent.

entries.name: Cracked component
entries.codex: Mech status, global rule. When a hit gets past shield and takes at least a quarter of maximum hull in one blow, the mech's die is rolled and the component it lands on is injured. An intact component cracks: it loses its keywords, crit chance and unique effect, but still does its basic action. Counterplay is shield before a big telegraphed hit. A cracked component stays cracked across skirmishes and battles until repaired in the hangar.

design.fantasy: They got through the armour and something important is bent.
design.holes: Threshold is a placeholder. Repair cost and the hangar screen are not built.

entries.name: Destroyed component
entries.codex: Mech status. When an injury lands on a component that is already cracked, it is destroyed: blank, it does nothing when it comes up, until the hangar repairs or replaces it. An injury that lands on a destroyed component or an empty hardpoint finds nothing to break, so a badly broken mech shrugs off more of them.

design.fantasy: Hit where it was already broken.

entries.name: Locked
entries.codex: Die status. See the lock keyword.

design.fantasy: Held for next round.

entries.name: Front rank
entries.codex: Three slots. Front-preferring foes fill these first. Always in line of fire.

design.fantasy: The bodies.

entries.name: Back rank
entries.codex: Three slots behind the front. Back-preferring foes hold these and never step up. Front-preferring foes wait here and step up when the slot ahead empties.

design.fantasy: The problems.

entries.name: Exposed
entries.codex: A back-rank foe is exposed when the front slot in its column is empty. Exposed foes are in line of fire.

design.fantasy: Kill the ghoul and the necromancer behind it is suddenly very interested in cover.

entries.name: Squad pool
entries.codex: Foes not yet on the field. Empty slots refill from the pool after each round. The skirmish is won when the field and the pool are both empty.

design.fantasy: There are always more where those came from.
design.holes: Elites should surface at set points rather than in pool order.

entries.name: Step up
entries.codex: After the dead are cleared, a front-preferring foe in the back rank moves into an empty front slot in its column.

design.fantasy: The horde closes the gap.

entries.name: Danger close
entries.codex: Indirect fire on the front rank removes shield from the firing mech equal to half the component's power, rounded up.

design.fantasy: You mortared the thing in your face. Your shields are now also in your face.

entries.name: Massive
entries.codex: A massive foe fills both slots of a column and counts as front rank. Its column is never exposed while it stands. Only some elites and bosses are massive.

design.fantasy: Too big for one slot. Too big for one anything.
design.holes: Cleave treats it as a front-rank neighbour; pierce cannot hit anything behind it because nothing is.

entries.name: Withdraw
entries.codex: Available at the start of any round after the first, before any component is spent, so there is never free damage. Ends the skirmish; survivors on both sides carry their damage to the battlefield.

design.fantasy: Enough. Fall back and let the map decide the rest.

entries.name: Movespeed
entries.codex: Movement points per phase. Entering a hex costs its terrain's move cost for that unit's traits.

design.fantasy: How much ground it covers before the enemy moves.

entries.name: Intent
entries.codex: Each squad's path for the phase is previewed exactly. It heads for the gate or the nearest city defense, or hunts mechs if aggro. Player routes resolve first.

design.fantasy: You can see where they are going. Whether they get there is up to you.
design.holes: Aggro is a fixed flag. Should be a behaviour per foe type.

entries.name: Body block
entries.codex: A squad stops at the first hex on its path occupied by a blocking unit. Flyers do not block; squads pass through their hex but never land on it.

design.fantasy: Stand in the road. They stop.

entries.name: Contact
entries.codex: After all movement, every connected group of adjacent units that contains both sides becomes one skirmish. Multiple skirmishes resolve one at a time.

design.fantasy: Adjacent means fighting.
design.holes: No participant cap. May need one for phone readability.

entries.name: Squad
entries.codex: An enemy hex is a squad: one foe type times a strength. A skirmish's enemy composition is whatever squads are chained together at contact, so the rift's formation and the player's disruption of it decide what you fight. Bosses are single three-hex units.

design.fantasy: One hex, one kind of thing, several of them.

entries.name: Footprint
entries.codex: A unit covers one or more hexes. A boss covers three in a triangle. Every footprint hex blocks, touches for contact, and is a tap target. Squads and mechs stay single-hex.

design.fantasy: Some things do not fit in a hex.
design.holes: Footprints do not rotate with facing.

entries.name: Structure
entries.codex: Gate and rift hexes are structures wider than one hex. Nobody stands on them. A squad whose path reaches any gate hex strikes the gate.

design.fantasy: The gate is not a hex. It is a wall.
design.holes: The rift does nothing yet beyond marking where squads spawn.

entries.name: Spawn
entries.codex: When Rift Pressure fills, the next squad of the faction's spawn list appears on the nearest free hex to the rift.

design.fantasy: The rift coughs up another squad.
design.holes: A full spawn list should arrive together as a formation; pressure currently sends one squad at a time.

entries.name: Plain
entries.codex: Cost 1.

design.fantasy: Open ground.

entries.name: Road
entries.codex: Cost 1.

design.fantasy: Somebody paved this before the end of the world.
design.holes: Tanks should move faster on roads. Not coded.

entries.name: Rough
entries.codex: Cost 2. Cost 1 for quads and flyers.

design.fantasy: Rubble and broken ground.

entries.name: Ruins
entries.codex: Cost 2. Cost 1 for quads and flyers.

design.fantasy: What is left of the suburbs.
design.holes: Designed as cover for the squad inside a skirmish. Skirmish terrain conditions are not coded.

entries.name: Water
entries.codex: Impassable except for hover and flyer.

design.fantasy: Deep enough to drown a tank.
design.holes: Designed to dampen burn inside a skirmish. Not coded.

entries.name: Mountain
entries.codex: Impassable except for flyer.

design.fantasy: Go around.

entries.name: Flyer
entries.codex: Ignores terrain cost, crosses water and mountains, cannot body-block.

design.fantasy: Reaches anywhere. Holds nothing.

entries.name: Hover
entries.codex: Crosses water.

design.fantasy: Skims the river like it is not there.

entries.name: Walker
entries.codex: Rough and ruins cost 1.

design.fantasy: Legs do not care about rubble.

entries.name: Tank
entries.codex: No effect yet.

design.fantasy: Tracks and armour.
design.holes: Intended: faster on roads.

entries.name: City defense
entries.codex: A static player-side unit. Squads path toward it, and it joins any skirmish it is adjacent to.

design.fantasy: The city shoots back.
design.holes: Defenses have no die. They cannot act inside a skirmish yet.

entries.name: On attack
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires after the damage roll on every attack. Effects: multiply or add damage or heat, or set a minimum damage. An effect may carry a when condition: component_cracked (only when the component being spent is cracked).

design.fantasy: Whenever this mech fires.

entries.name: On shield gain
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this mech gains shield from any source.

design.fantasy: Whenever plating goes up.

entries.name: On heat gain
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this mech gains heat.

design.fantasy: Whenever the reactor runs hotter.

entries.name: On round start
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires after the roll, before rerolls.

design.fantasy: As the dice come up.

entries.name: On skirmish start
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires once when the skirmish begins.

design.fantasy: As contact is made.

entries.name: On crit
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when an attack component crits. Effects: multiply or add damage, add burn to the target, vent the attacker's heat.

design.fantasy: When the round finds the seam.

entries.name: On hull damage
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this mech loses hull.

design.fantasy: When they get through.
design.holes: Hook for the pinned berserker idea.

entries.name: Out of combat
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires at the end of a battlefield phase in which this mech had no skirmish.

design.fantasy: A phase spent not fighting.

entries.name: Command die
entries.codex: One die rolled alongside the mech dice each round. Its entries are rechargeable commander abilities and never deal damage. They come from the hangar, never from rewards. Die size is a research path.

design.fantasy: You are not in the machine. You are the one telling the machines what to do.
design.holes: Open question: whether the command die exists at all, or one-shots only.

entries.name: One-shot
entries.codex: Consumable ability. Pouch of three. Picked up from skirmishes, expires when the battle ends. Starting stock restocks every battle.

design.fantasy: The button you only get to press once.

entries.name: Reward pick
entries.codex: After a skirmish victory: a modifier on a component you carry, a one-shot, or a battle-wide boon. Weighted by the squad's faction.

design.fantasy: Three things on the table. Take one.

entries.name: City ability
entries.codex: Battlefield-level ability owned and upgraded by the city: sprint, airlift, teleport, tractor beam, orbital strike. Cooldowns measured in phases.

design.fantasy: The city has a very large gun and a very large crane.
design.holes: Consider range limits from the gate so the push north leaves support behind.

entries.name: Cooldown
entries.codex: City abilities only. Counted in battlefield phases. Never used inside a skirmish.

design.fantasy: Reloading. Come back in two phases.

entries.name: Component
entries.codex: A piece of equipment on a mech, and one entry on its die. There is no generic equipment: every entry on a die is a component, or an empty hardpoint. Each round the die is rolled and the component that comes up is what the mech can do.

design.fantasy: The gun, the plate, the heat sink. What the machine is made of, and what the die shows.
design.holes: Multi-slot components were considered and scrapped on 18 September as invisible complexity.

entries.name: Hardpoint
entries.codex: A free slot on the chassis. Any component fits any hardpoint. On the model a hardpoint is a socket where the component mounts.

design.fantasy: Bolt it on. The chassis does not care what.

entries.name: Fixed component
entries.codex: A component built into the chassis: always on the die, never removed, never sold, and it uses no hardpoint. The Badger's claw and its plating are fixed.

design.fantasy: The part of the machine that is the machine. Restriction makes the build.
design.holes: Decided against unlocking fixed slots for money (18 September).

entries.name: Empty hardpoint
entries.codex: A hardpoint with nothing in it is an entry on the die that does nothing when it comes up. Nothing fills it for you.

design.fantasy: You ran light. The die remembers.

entries.name: on_injury
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when an injury lands on a component. Effects: no_destroy (a cracked component holds instead of being destroyed).

design.fantasy: What the machine does when something inside it breaks.
